title: Attribution vector file
description: One file in contracts/attribution/attribution-vectors/ is a JSON array of cases, split by subject. Every case is a pure function input and its expected credit, so the engine in the app is built against this file rather than the other way round: a case states the outcome a reviewer would defend, and adding a model case means adding a case here, never a test in the code. The credits of one case always sum exactly to the conversion value, because the largest-remainder residual goes to the last touch.

name.description: What the case proves, phrased as an assertion.

model.description: The attribution model, chosen per campaign. It is the model of the owning campaign: the campaign of the last click in the chain.

window_days.description: The owning campaign's attribution window. A click is inside the window when it is not after the conversion and no more than this many days before it, counted as 24-hour periods from `conversion.at`.

currency.description: The ISO 4217 code that decides the fraction digits of every credit: 2 for USD, 0 for VND.

at.description: When the conversion happened, in UTC.

value.description: The conversion value as a decimal string, never a binary float, so 100.00 keeps its two fraction digits.

chain.description: The touchpoints, oldest first. The engine filters it to the clicks inside the window whose traffic class is HUMAN, and a BOT or SUSPECT click is never credited. An empty chain means the conversion is unattributed.

expect.description: The credits, one per credited click, as decimal strings at the currency's fraction digits. The sum is exactly the conversion value. An empty array means the conversion is UNATTRIBUTED.

expected_credit_status.description: Optional. When absent the runner derives it: `COMPUTED` when `expect` is not empty, `UNATTRIBUTED` otherwise.

reason.description: Optional. Why the conversion is unattributed, such as `no_chain`, `all_clicks_outside_window` or `bot_only`. Present only where the empty `expect` needs an explanation a reviewer would ask for.

click_id.description: The click's identity. A case never repeats one.

link_id.description: The link the click came through.

campaign_id.description: The campaign the link belongs to. A chain may span campaigns; the last click's campaign owns the conversion.

at.description: When the click happened, in UTC.

traffic_class.description: Only HUMAN clicks are credited. BOT is a crawler or a link-preview fetcher; SUSPECT is a visitor over the per-link click rate.

click_id.description: The credited click, naming an entry of `chain`.

credit.description: The credited amount as a decimal string at the currency's fraction digits.
